one_liner: Header-only C++14/17/20 ranges library (basis of std::ranges); one bug-report benchmark beat an unshown hand-rolled loop by 3-13%.
what_it_does: Range-v3 adds composable, lazy views (transform, filter, reverse, concat, join, zip and more), eager actions (sort, unique and similar, piped onto containers) and range overloads of the STL algorithms, all usable from C++14 onward. Pipelines are written left to right with the pipe syntax (rng | views::transform(f) | views::common) and materialized either with a container's iterator-pair constructor or with ranges::to. It is not a drop-in container or algorithm replacement: it lives in namespace ranges and is the library C++20 std::ranges was standardized from, with more adaptors than the standard has.
how_it_is_fast: Views are lazy adaptors, so a transform/filter pipeline runs as one pass over the source with no intermediate containers. In the cited benchmark, views::common over a transform of a std::vector yields sized random-access iterators, so std::vector's iterator-pair constructor can size the result once and move-construct each transformed string into it; why this beat the unshown hand-rolled version is not explained (allocation strategy is a likely factor, inference). Where range-v3 loses, the cause is iterator abstraction the optimizer cannot see through: view_adaptor passing iterators by reference (issue #668), concat's variant-based iterator (issue #1081), and the extra end-of-range checks of pull-based filter and join that push-based designs such as transrangers avoid.
when_to_use: C++14 or C++17 codebases that want C++20-style composable views and range algorithms before they can move to std::ranges.
Code that needs pieces std::ranges lacks, such as actions (eager in-place container algorithms) or views::cache1 to stop a transform being re-evaluated.

Simple single-pass pipelines (transform and filter over contiguous data) materialized through views::common and the container's iterator-pair constructor, the shape that matched or beat hand-rolled code in issue #1337.
Writing expressive code first and then benchmarking hot spots, which is the maintainer's own advice in issue #668.
when_not_to_use: Hot loops built on views::concat or views::join: issue #1081 (open) has a 2021 report of about 11,800 ms with concat against about 630 ms without it at -O3 on Clang 11.0.2, issue #700 ('view::join is quite slow') is open, and the transrangers README reports range-v3 doing very badly on a concat|take|filter|transform test on Clang, GCC and Visual Studio.
Materializing with ranges::to in a hot path: issue #1337 (open since 2019) measured it about 1.8x (-O2) to 2.2x (-O3) slower than the hand-rolled version.
Debug builds and build-time-sensitive projects: a debug repro in #1081 took about 36 s with concat against 2.5 s without, and compile-time complaints appear in #758 and #1241.
Projects that need API stability: the README promises no long-term stability outside the ranges::cpp20 namespace, and the last tagged release is 0.12.0 from June 2022.

integration.dependencies: none (packaged in vcpkg, Conan and build2; CMake target range-v3::range-v3)
integration.min_toolchain: C++14; clang 6+, GCC 7+, Clang/LLVM 6+ on Windows, Visual Studio 2019+ with /permissive- and /std:c++17 or later
integration.platforms: any platform with a supported compiler
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the algorithms keep iterator overloads like <algorithm> and add range overloads, but views, actions and ranges::to are a different interface in namespace ranges, not std

gotchas: Views are lazy and re-evaluate on dereference: a filter after a transform calls the transform function again for every element that passes (issue #1090); insert views::cache1 after an expensive transform.

Views are non-owning, so lifetimes are the caller's problem: issue #964 is a heap-use-after-free with view::transform, zip_with and lambdas, and in #1081 a maintainer points out lambdas returning dangling views of lvalue containers.

In #1337 the views::common plus iterator-pair-constructor form was the fast one and ranges::to the slow one. Current ranges::to reserves and then assigns when the range is sized (conversion.hpp), but no newer measurement shows whether that closes the gap, and the issue is still open.

The repo's perf/range_conversion.cpp benchmark appends 2,856,000 words (476,000 x 6) in every fixture SetUp and never clears them. Google Benchmark calls SetUp before every run, so the input grows across its iteration-probing runs and can differ between the RangeCommon and RangeTo fixtures; its numbers (201.5 ms against 241.6 ms) are indicative only.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued siblings does the same job: svector, plf::colony, veque, EASTL and the other entries are containers, while range-v3 builds and transforms sequences that feed any of them. Pick it for lazy pipelines on pre-C++20 compilers or for adaptors std::ranges lacks; the 'sequence-containers' category is a poor fit, and the existing 'ranges-and-views' category matches better.
verified_claims_summary: In issue #1337 (opened 2019-09-29), a reporter used Google Benchmark on a 2-CPU 2684 MHz machine with an unnamed compiler to time a palindrome-marking views::transform | views::common pipeline over about 476k words, copied into std::vector<std::string>. It took 10.8 ms against 12.4 ms for an unshown 'handrolled' version at -O2 (13% less time) and 9.31 ms against 9.59 ms at -O3 (3%, near noise), and was about 2.4x faster than an unshown 'algorithm' version; the ranges::to variant was 1.8x to 2.2x slower than hand-rolled, which is the issue's actual subject. The maintainer's re-run only compared the range_common and range_to forms, with a harness whose input grows between runs.
status_note: Active (commits through 2026-10-10, 4.4k stars), but the last tag is 0.12.0 from June 2022; it is BSL-1.0, header-only and packaged in vcpkg, Conan and build2, with no stability promise outside ranges::cpp20.
